title: Cutting & Sorting Data ✂️
description: Extract columns with cut, order lines with sort, and remove duplicates with uniq.

slides.title: The `cut` Command ✂️
slides.content:
## Slice and Dice Text

`cut` extracts sections from each line of a file:
- `-d` – delimiter (default TAB).
- `-f` – field number(s) to extract (e.g., `-f1,3` or `-f1-3`).
- `-c` – character positions.

Example: `cut -d: -f1,7 /etc/passwd` (username and shell).

quizData.question: What would `cut -d, -f2 data.csv` do?

options.text: Print only the second comma‑separated field

quizData.explanation: `-d,` sets comma as delimiter; `-f2` extracts the second field.

slides.title: Sorting with `sort` 📊
slides.content:
## Bring Order to Chaos

`sort` sorts lines alphabetically or numerically:
- `-n` – numeric sort.
- `-r` – reverse order.
- `-k` – sort by a specific column (e.g., `-k2`).
- `-t` – field delimiter.
- `-u` – unique (remove duplicates; but `uniq` is more common).

quizData.question: `sort` without options arranges lines in reverse alphabetical order.
quizData.explanation: Default sort is ascending alphabetical (A–Z, a–z).

slides.title: Removing Duplicates with `uniq` 🧹
slides.content:
## Only Adjacent Lines

`uniq` filters out repeated lines that are **adjacent**. Often paired with `sort`:
- `sort file | uniq` – returns unique lines.
- `-c` – prefix lines with count of occurrences.
- `-d` – only print duplicate lines.
- `-u` – only print unique (non‑duplicate) lines.
